items.title: feat(id): id.device.v1 MQTT device bridge spec + labelled PoC (#2343)
items.body: Closes #2343. ## What The `id.device.v1` MQTT device-bridge **spec plus a labelled PoC**, exactly the remainder scoped by #2343's 2026-11-08 triage. Nothing here is production firmware or a production bridge. - **`doc/2026-11-09T05-00-00Z_feature_mqtt_device_bridge_id_device_v1/`** — the schema doc: topic table, per-world prefix, one connection per device, example documents for manifest / wants / cap-result / surface / events, wire bounds, and the recorded recommendations (retention, TLS + per-device credentials, reconnect/backoff, device-side journaling, minimum `time.tick`, closed firmware subset). - **`pkgs/id/src/device_bridge.rs`** — the PoC module (labelled as such in its module docs): topic helpers, fail-closed `Authenticator`, `Bridge::evaluate_wants` with the web refusal vocabulary, `FakeBroker` (retained manifest, retained-wants ban, wire bounds, auth), `FakeDevice` (journal across reconnects, 1 Hz tick floor, capped exponential backoff, encoder-as-`Key` with a signed delta). A real MQTT transport replaces `FakeBroker` without touching `Bridge` — that seam is the point of the PoC. ## Decisions reused from #5901 (not reopened) Retained manifest only · TLS plus per-device credentials · closed device subset (`device.info`, small `screen`/`text`, closed `form.*`, `loc.position` when GNSS present, key/encoder events) · bridge as translator. #2028 still defers production rollout; #5783 owns boards, firmware, OTA and power. Home Assistant interop is recorded as out-of-scope-but-supported. ## Bounds Reuses the host constants rather than restating them: 64 KiB `wants`/events, 8 KiB args. One finding worth noting: oversize args are rejected by `parse_wants` at parse time, before any per-request evaluation — the PoC test asserts that host boundary instead of inventing a per-request code that the host never emits. ## Tests ``` cargo test --lib device_bridge # 11 passed ``` Covering: topic shape, retained manifest for late subscribers, the full manifest→wants→result flow, unknown cap, ungranted cap, retained-wants rejection, oversize wants, oversize args at the host parse boundary, fail-closed auth (wrong token, unknown device, unauthenticated publish), minimum tick, backoff monotonicity/cap, encoder-to-`Key` delta. No production code paths are modified: `lib.rs` gains one `pub mod` line. items.title: docs(id): decision record for ESP32 hardware platform line (#5783)
items.body: Design-only record for #5783 (task 14116). Adds `doc/2026-11-09_design_id5783.md` — the first landed artifact for this issue. No production code. Covers, per the packet acceptance: - Board posture: one ESP32-S3 reference + compatibility envelope, measured against the bridge 64 KiB frame budget (§1, heap-margin invariant I-9). - Identity provisioning: device-owned identity via the #5884 ceremony, destroy-on-reset, stolen-device knowledge bounded by ceiling (§2). - Firmware lifecycle: flake-reproducible builds, offline-signed images, A/B OTA over HTTPS with rollback to last-good, checksummed device-side journal inherited from #2343 (§3). - Power: mains-first reference, battery as measured envelope, wake-storm avoidance as fleet property via per-device-seeded jittered backoff (§4). - Field behaviour: no-RTC untimed mode with bridge-assigned ingest time, bounded store-and-forward with gap signals, no portal click-through, two-slot checksummed writes (§5). - Open questions settled with named defaults: Q1 Rust/esp-idf + shared workspace crates; Q2 ESPHome interop-only; Q3 fake-device gates, bench informs; Q4 bench-first, reproducible-by-construction. - Invariants I-1–I-10; rejected alternatives with reasons; parent/sibling decisions (#2343, #5686, #5684/#5884, #5671) consumed, not re-decided (one correction: the setup-ceremony record is open PR #7850 for #5884, not merged — recorded accurately in the doc). Evidence baseline in the record header. Follows the `doc/YYYY-MM-DD_design_idNNNN.md` convention (cf. #5781, #5804). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? ### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>tokio-rs/tracing (tracing-subscriber)</summary>

### [`v0.3.17`](https://togithub.com/tokio-rs/tracing/releases/tag/tracing-subscriber-0.3.17): tracing-subscriber 0.3.17

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/tokio-rs/tracing/compare/tracing-subscriber-0.3.16...tracing-subscriber-0.3.17)

This release of `tracing-subscriber` fixes a build error when using `env-filter`
with recent versions of the `regex` crate. It also introduces several minor API
improvements.

##### Fixed

-   **env-filter**: Add "unicode-case" and "unicode-perl" to the `regex`
    dependency, fixing a build error with recent versions of `regex` ([#​2566])
-   A number of minor documentation typos and other fixes ([#​2384], [#​2378],
    [#​2368], [#​2548])

##### Added

-   **filter**: Add `fmt::Display` impl for `filter::Targets` ([#​2343])
-   **fmt**: Made `with_ansi(false)` no longer require the "ansi" feature, so that
    ANSI formatting escapes can be disabled without requiring ANSI-specific
    dependencies ([#​2532])

##### Changed

-   **fmt**: Dim targets in the `Compact` formatter, matching the default
    formatter ([#​2409])
